reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Re-extracted the adopted rules and checked the dated broad-track catalogue and course prerequisites independently of the frozen comparison, then reconsidered all matches and the selected workbook evidence.
findings: The broad track has 60 EC per year across 22 credit-bearing components. The workshop is non-credit. Completing year one meets binding advice and the 45 EC course-entry floor. EU Law precedes both courses that require it. The mandatory exchange is 30 EC with approved courses and a law-credit minimum. By thesis enrolment the student can have 120 compulsory EC and the required seminar and first-year passes.

The arbitration exercise in Transnational Business Law is a closer counterpart to Groningen’s commercial dispute work than to specialist conflict-of-laws doctrine. The political science approach to international institutions gives a partial counterpart to Law, Power and Politics. The technology option has real technical and ethics content while leaving specialist technology law and competition doctrine visible as gaps.

The two workbook-backed plans have distinct emphases and share the legal sequence. Course labels, explanatory notes, source links and the thesis-adjacent optional research element agree with the reviewed evidence.
